transcript:
Header: 2025-12-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood CSM); Maya Thompson (Paragon Head of Security), Priya Nair (Paragon Legal), Liam O'Connor (Procurement), Ethan Brooks (CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick legal review of MSA/DPA, confirm security docs, discuss SLA liability cap and vendor onboarding timeline. Action items captured.

00:00 - 00:23 Ava Chen: Hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, joining with Diego our SE and Nina from CSM. How's everyone doing?
00:24 - 00:41 Maya Thompson: Doing well thanks. We got the MSA and DPA last night, Priya and I skimmed, wanted to go through a few open items and align on timeline for signatures.
00:42 - 01:10 Ava Chen: Great, that's the plan. We'll run through the redlines you flagged. Diego will cover any technical questions (private deployments, VPC, KMS) and Nina will help with onboarding timelines and contacts.
01:11 - 01:48 Priya Nair: First item is indemnification and liability cap language — our legal team needs clarity on the cap relative to annual spend; there's also a carve-out request for regulatory fines.
01:49 - 02:16 Diego Morales: On the tech side, we also want to confirm where logs live, retention, and can we opt for on-prem ingestion or a VPC endpoint. Our Redwood Private solution supports customer-managed VPC and HSM/KMS integrations, but I'll let Ava touch on contractual pieces.
02:17 - 02:45 Ava Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and customer-managed network. In the MSA we typically have a liability cap tied to fees paid over 12 months — we can discuss thresholds. For regulatory fines, we generally don't cover those but we can look at language.
02:46 - 03:19 Priya Nair: Also: data residency and DPA exhibit — we need explicit language for EU data subjects, and a vendor subprocessor list. Will you provide that?
03:20 - 03:52 Ava Chen: Absolutely. We'll include the subprocessor list and an exhibit for data locality. We can provide the DPA exhibit with EU addendum and standard clauses. We'll also share our list of subprocessors and a SOC2 report.
03:53 - 04:25 Maya Thompson: Can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit details, and whether Redwood keeps any persistent logs we can't control? That's a big one for us.
04:26 - 05:00 Diego Morales: Encryption at rest is customer-managed for Private via KMS; for hosted APIs we use provider-managed encryption but support customer-managed keys in dedicated/private deployments. Regarding logs: we can configure retention and streaming of audit logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3. There may be short-term application logs for debugging but we can agree retention windows in the DPA.
05:01 - 05:33 Ethan Brooks: On the SLA, what uptime and credits do you offer? Procurement was surprised by the 99.9% baseline in the quote — we need clear escalation and SRE contact.
05:34 - 06:05 Ava Chen: Our standard SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% with credits; for mission-critical we offer higher tiers with contractual commitments — we can table an enterprise SLA with targeted P1 response times and a named escalation path. We'll include SRE contacts in the contract annex.
06:06 - 06:41 Liam O'Connor: Pricing — procurement needs a clear worksheet with committed vs burst pricing and the renewal terms. Also approval process: do you accept net-45 PO? Any discounts for annual commitments?
06:42 - 07:10 Ava Chen: We can accept net-30 or net-45 for enterprise, depends on account. Discounts available for 12/24 month committed reserved capacity—Diego will share the pricing worksheet with examples of unit economics and a committed discount table.
07:11 - 07:48 Priya Nair: Back to the DPA — can you confirm breach notification timelines and subprocessor change notices? We require 72-hour notification and 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors where feasible.
07:49 - 08:20 Ava Chen: We commit to 72-hour breach notifications. For subprocessors we'll provide reasonable notice and the subprocessor list; if there's a critical change we'll loop in your security team.
08:21 - 09:05 Diego Morales: Technical note: if you want an on-prem package for regulated workloads we can produce an air-gapped bundle but that requires procurement and infra planning — typically a longer lead time and different support SLAs.
09:06 - 09:38 Maya Thompson: Good to know. For now we'd prefer VPC/private deployment in our cloud region. Also, do you support HSM-backed keys for tokenization and KV cache encryption?
09:39 - 10:08 Diego Morales: Yes, HSM-backed via customer KMS is supported for Private deployments. I will include a runbook for KV cache handling, eviction policies, and how we handle prefix caching to avoid leakage.
10:09 - 10:45 Priya Nair: Indemnity again — can you provide a vendor insurance certificate? Our risk team needs to validate limits.
10:46 - 11:11 Ava Chen: Yes, we can provide an insurance certificate showing commercial general liability and cyber insurance. We'll put that in the security pack.
11:12 - 12:02 Ethan Brooks: For onboarding — what's the timeline from signature to production? We need a playbook for pilot, benchmarking, and go-live.
12:03 - 12:44 Nina Park: Typical timeline: signature -> provision dedicated capacity (1-2 weeks depending on region and GPU availability) -> 2 week POC/benchmark -> integration -> go-live. We'll provide a vendor onboarding checklist and runbook.
12:45 - 13:20 Liam O'Connor: Procurement wants the full contract package for finance review — final MSA, DPA, SOW, pricing worksheet so they can start approvals. They need it no later than Dec 10 to hit our board cycle.
13:21 - 14:02 Ava Chen: Understood — we'll aim to get redlines and docs to Priya and Liam by Dec 8. Diego will share pricing and benchmark plan by Dec 9.
14:03 - 14:50 Priya Nair: A couple of smaller items — export controls clause, subcontractor liability, and data deletion confirmation at termination. We'll mark those in the redline.
14:51 - 15:30 Diego Morales: Quick technical clarification — if you want to run privacy-sensitive subsets in your VPC we recommend isolating the KV caches per customer workspace and we can show cost tradeoffs for multi-tenant vs dedicated cache.
15:31 - 16:12 Maya Thompson: Sounds good. Also, do you have FedRAMP or other gov cloud readiness? We may have some public sector customers later.
16:13 - 16:45 Ava Chen: We don't currently hold FedRAMP, but we can discuss path to compliance. For now we can support VPC/on-prem patterns to meet many regulatory obligations.
16:46 - 17:30 Liam O'Connor: On signatures — will redlines be acceptable or do you want to handle via table of exceptions? Procurement prefers a consolidated list of exceptions to speed review.
17:31 - 18:10 Priya Nair: Yes consolidated exceptions is fine — we'll provide a single doc with clause numbers and proposed language.
18:11 - 19:05 Ava Chen: Great. To recap: we'll send redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2/ISO certs, insurance cert, pricing worksheet, and benchmark runbook. We'll aim for docs by Dec 8-9 and schedule a signature call week of Dec 15.
19:06 - 19:45 Ethan Brooks: One last thing on metrics — can you provide an SLO table for token latency p50/p95 for the recommended Dedicated sizes? We'll need that for SLAs.
19:46 - 20:20 Diego Morales: Yes I'll add p50/p95 numbers and include expected throughput per GPU config. Also note quantization and batching tradeoffs — higher throughput lowers latency variance but it depends on prompt shapes.
20:21 - 21:00 Ava Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links: redlined contract (shared drive link), pricing worksheet (link), SOC2 (secure link), and SE runbook (link).
21:01 - 21:30 Maya Thompson: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. Looking forward to the docs.
21:31 - 21:45 Ava Chen: Thanks all, talk soon.

References shared: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (SOC2), https://redwood.example.com/pricing/worksheet-CRM-45832 (pricing worksheet), shared drive: Paragon-Redwood-MSA-DPA-redline.docx

End of transcript.
